title: Tenant ingest handshake and adaptive latency sagas for VPC/on-prem observability
creator: Aisha Karim
description:
Problem: Private and Dedicated customers deploy local collectors and perimeter relays that must deliver traces, metrics, and logs without risking cross-tenant contamination, while maintaining latency SLOs and debuggability. Current ad-hoc collectors sometimes cause spikes in ingest latency or silent data loss under backpressure, leaving customers blind during incidents.

Goal: Design and implement a tenant-bounded ingest handshake and adaptive latency saga across VPC/on-prem collectors and Redwood ingest. Deliver a robust protocol for capacity discovery, signed tenant envelopes, lease-based temporary routing, and active backpressure signals. Couple this with an adaptive sampling/retention controller that prioritizes low-latency traces and critical error logs for SLO-sensitive tenants, and surface latency/error dashboards in Console.

Non-goals: Full rewrite of existing collectors, replacing customer-managed network appliances, or changing model of how customers ship logs to our perimeter (we operate above the network transport layer).
acceptance_criteria: Handshake protocol implemented between perimeter collector and Redwood ingress with mutual auth and per-tenant lease tokens
Ingest pipeline enforces tenant envelope validation and rejects cross-tenant attribution with audit logs
Adaptive latency controller reduces tail latency by at least 25% under synthetic backpressure workloads while preserving >=90% of P99 error traces for high-sensitivity tenants
Console dashboards show per-tenant ingest latency distribution, dropped/retained trace ratios, and an alerting rule for lease expiration and sudden sampling shifts
Canary rollout on one Dedicated customer cluster with rollback plan and runbook
Automated e2e test harness that simulates bursty on-prem traffic and verifies lease renewal, backpressure signals, and sampling behavior
technical_plan:
Phase 1: Protocol + Validation
- Define a lightweight TCP/HTTP handshake: collector presents signed collector identity, tenant-list token, and desired ingress QoS. Redwood responds with a short-lived lease token, initial sampling policy, and ingress shard assignment.
- Enveloping: collectors MUST wrap traces/metrics/logs in a tenant-signed envelope (tenant id + lease token + sequence watermark). Ingest validates envelope signature and sequence monotonicity before accepting.
- Backpressure signals: implement HTTP 429 with structured Retry-After and a X-Redwood-Backoff-Token header that maps to leasing.

Phase 2: Adaptive latency saga & sampling controller
- Implement a latency SLO inspector in the ingest tier that computes per-tenant tail percentiles and issues policy updates every 5s.
- Sampling controller applies three levers: priority-preserving deterministic sampling for traces with errors or long spans, time-window emergent retention for metrics, and ephemeral buffering with tenant watermarks.
- Controller communicates policy deltas via short-lived lease renewal responses to the collector.

Phase 3: Observability + Rollout
- Ingest side emits internal traces about handshake lifecycles, rejected envelopes, and sampling deltas (tagged tenant-safe).
- Console exposes dashboards: tenant-ingest-latency, tenant-drop-ratio, handshake-success-rate, lease-expiry-alerts. Add alert thresholds and runbooks.
- Canary: deploy to Dedicated cluster A, run synthetic burst tests, observe dashboards, iterate.

Implementation notes: use existing collector identity PKI (expand cert claims), reuse KV cache for ephemeral lease lookup, and piggyback policy updates on existing control channel to avoid creating a new persistent socket.
tradeoffs: Signed envelopes add CPU overhead on collectors and ingest; mitigated by batching signature verifications and caching verified leases
Lease tokens introduce slight complexity for offline collectors; we support a short grace window but that opens a small replay surface we mitigate with sequence watermarks
Aggressive adaptive sampling reduces cost and latency but risks missing rare signals; mitigated by deterministic retention for error traces and explicit customer opt-ins for full fidelity
Incremental rollout favored over big-bang to limit blast radius for private deployments
